reason: Machine lens: CMP abs,X (DD), BEQ, BCS are all real 65SC12 opcodes; no Rockwell bit ops. Old at DF29: LDA sky_ry,X (BD, 3 bytes, 4c) + CMP sky_stop (C5, 2b, 3c) + BCC no (2b) = 7 bytes; new CMP sky_ry,X (3b, 4c) + BEQ (2b) + BCS no (2b) = 7 bytes, so .no stays at DF48 and nothing after moves. sky_ry = &BCB4, X < SKY_ROWS = 6, so BCB4+X never crosses a page (no +1 either side). Recount: stop<ry 9 -> 8 (BEQ, BCS not taken); stop==ry 9 -> 7 (BEQ taken to DF30, same page, +1 only); stop>ry ('no') 10 -> 9 (BCS taken DF2E->DF48, same page, offset +&18 in range). Condition: old exits iff ry < stop; new exits iff C=1 and Z=0 of stop-ry, i.e. stop > ry: identical, unsigned. Only A differs (stop vs ry): the next instruction LDA sky_rl,X overwrites it on the pass path; on the no path SEC RTS and both callers (sky_col_check, sky_col_zero in sky_edges) go to .next (INX/CPX) without reading A. No self-modified operands, no entries past sky_col_row, no label+N references, code in HAZEL not read as data; skyrow_eq is local inside the { } block. Saves 1 cycle per execution (2 in the equal case), 0 bytes.
